rules.title: Return only the fields the client uses
rules.what: APIs return only the fields the consuming client uses; clients can narrow the projection (sparse fieldsets, GraphQL selection, ?fields=), and the default projection is minimal.
rules.why: Every unused field is serialised, transferred, parsed and dropped on every call: pure friction between the server and the user's battery.
rules.how: Define minimal default projections; offer field selection parameters; deprecate overweight endpoints after checking real usage.

verify.how: Payload size per endpoint within the stated budget; unused fields identified by client usage and removed.

limits: Public API contracts restrict removal; deprecation policy applies.

rules.title: Compression and caching headers on responses
rules.what: Compressible responses are compressed (gzip/brotli); cacheable responses carry correct Cache-Control/ETag headers so clients and CDNs do not re-fetch.
rules.why: These headers cost one line and avoid re-transferring the same bytes to the same clients on every call; they are the highest leverage-to-effort ratio on an API.
rules.how: Enable response compression for text content types; set Cache-Control with explicit max-age per resource type; ETag/Last-Modified for conditional requests.

verify.how: Curl/production check: Content-Encoding on compressible responses, Cache-Control present, 304 on conditional re-request.

limits: Do not cache personalised or sensitive responses; private directive where needed.

rules.title: Batch over chatty exchanges
rules.what: Prefer batch or bulk endpoints over N individual calls for the same operation; design integration surfaces so the client can do one round trip instead of ten.
rules.why: Each call pays fixed costs: connection, TLS, headers, authentication, latency. Ten small calls cost more than one batch doing the same work.
rules.how: Provide batch/bulk variants for collection operations; allow the client to submit groups; document the maximum batch size.

patterns.note: await inside a loop; candidate for Promise.all or a batch endpoint.
HTTP call inside a loop; candidate for batching.

verify.how: Call count per integration task measured; within budget or batched.

limits: Sequential calls with real dependencies are not chatty; verify independence before batching.

rules.title: Rate limiting protects everyone's resources
rules.what: Public and expensive endpoints are rate-limited, with limits that protect the service and are documented to clients.
rules.why: Without limits, one abusive or faulty client spends the service's resources; with them, the failure stays at the boundary it belongs to. Retry clients need 429 with Retry-After to back off correctly.
rules.how: Per-key or per-IP limits on expensive paths; 429 with Retry-After; burst allowance; monitor the distribution.

verify.how: Load test over the limit: clean 429s, no resource exhaustion behind the limiter.

limits: Limits themselves cost a store (counter); size that infrastructure to the need.

rules.title: Version consciously
rules.what: Keep the number of live API versions to the minimum the contract requires; retire old versions on a published schedule.
rules.why: Every live version runs, is tested, documented and deployed forever. Version sprawl multiplies the whole service's cost for a shrinking audience.
rules.how: Publish deprecation dates, support overlap windows, provide migration notes; monitor old-version usage to schedule retirement.

verify.how: Live versions inventory with usage stats and retirement dates.

limits: Contractual obligations override retirement speed; they are recorded.

rules.title: Errors that are lightweight and useful
rules.what: Error responses carry a machine-readable code, a human-readable message and a correlation id; they are small, consistent and safe (no stack traces to clients).
rules.why: A verbose error (full stack, whole object dumps) costs bytes on the failure path and leaks internals; a useless one costs a retry or a support ticket, both more expensive than the response.
rules.how: One error envelope for the API; structured codes; log the details server-side with the correlation id.

verify.how: Error path responses: small, consistent, no internal details; correlation id present and resolvable in server logs.
